title: The CPU is back: Rethinking the CPU-GPU split for LLM inference
excerpt: Why agentic AI is driving the shift back to CPU inference.
content_html:
AI Developer Advocate

Developer Advocate

For the past 3 years, graphics processing units (GPUs) have dominated the large language model (LLM) conversation. In traditional chatbot applications, central processing units (CPUs) provide a fraction of the total compute per request, while GPUs do the heavy lifting. However, inference isn't a single model answering a single question. A growing reliance on tool calls, multistep reasoning, and orchestration across small, specialized models changes the math on where compute should live. Intel has called out this shift noting that the CPU-to-GPU ratio is moving from 1:8 in training workloads to 1:1, and in some cases 4:1 in agentic deployments.

Here we'll examine why the assumptions making GPUs the obvious choice for LLM inference are being renegotiated, what's driving renewed demand for CPU-based serving, and what the data says about where the industry is heading.

What CPUs are good at

At their core (no pun intended), CPUs and GPUs solve fundamentally different problems.

A modern GPU contains tens of thousands of cores designed to execute the same operation on thousands of data elements simultaneously. This makes them extraordinarily fast at the dense matrix multiplications that dominate the forward pass of a transformer for inference. During training, and during high-concurrency batched inference, that parallelism translates directly into throughput: greater tokens per second (TPS), and many more requests served per dollar of compute.

Modern CPUs, by contrast, have anywhere from one to hundreds of cores optimized for sequential, conditional, and branching logic. They're particularly fast at a single operation moving through a complex decision tree. They have direct access to main system memory, and they're the natural execution environment for the orchestration layer wrapping any model. Tool dispatch, code execution, Python runtimes, sandboxes, input/output (I/O), and the agent loop control flow all sit in the CPU.

These architectures, while different in nature, aren't competitors; they work best in tandem. The real question isn't which architecture is better, but which workload belongs where.

This division of labor comes down to how we measure their work: FLOPS versus instruction latency.

GPUs live and die by floating-point operations per second (FLOPS). Because AI models are massive webs of decimal numbers being multiplied and added, a GPU's job is to brute-force trillions of these matrix calculations simultaneously. It's built entirely for raw mathematical throughput.

CPUs, by contrast, specialize in instruction latency. Instruction latency measures how fast a single core can execute an unpredictable chain of diverse commands. A CPU core excels at the rapid logic shuffling needed to parse JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), handle network I/O, or check security permissions.

If you force a GPU to run a chaotic Python runtime, its massive FLOP capacity sits idle, choked by constant task-switching. If you force a CPU to crunch an LLM's math, it works perfectly, but takes ages because it lacks the massive parallel pipelines. The GPU is the mathematical muscle; the CPU is the logic engine directing the show.

The traditional inference stack: Where CPUs were passengers

When we think of the traditional inference stack, we think about the chatbot serving application. Here, the CPU often plays a supporting role.

A request arrives at the API server, where the CPU tokenizes and schedules it. The CPU handles all these initial tasks. It then hands the request to the GPU for the forward pass, which dominates the compute budget. The GPU runs attention, feeds forward layers, and samples the next token with a brief CPU sync to retrieve it and update the scheduler. It then repeats until an end-of-sequence token is emitted. Finally, the CPU collects the output and returns it to end the session.

In this model, the CPU acts as a receptionist, doing the coordination and organizational work, while the GPU does the computational heavy lifting. The ratio of CPUs to GPUs in AI data centers during the training era reflected this: roughly 1 to 2 CPUs for every 8 GPUs, a ratio dictated more by GPUs throughput than by CPU demand. Teams provisioned CPUs to keep GPUs fed. This setup is slowly shifting away from the de facto standard, as advancements in CPU inference increase global efficiency.

The first driver: How agents are changing the workload

With the rise of agentic AI comes a new inference profile magnifying the need for CPU-specific compute.

"Agentic AI" conjures up images of integrated agent harnesses, like Hermes and Openclaw, and developers with hosts of agents tied into their coding assistants. While these use cases are becoming more popular, agentic AI isn't as niche as it may seem at first glance. In fact, many people aren't using the "traditional" process of querying a chatbot. Popular AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT are backed by enormous models that often incorporate "reasoning" stages into their more complex responses. During reasoning, the "chatbot" becomes a full agentic system. A single user-visible task may decompose into dozens of individual model calls, each of which is short, context-dependent, and conditionally branching.

In an agentic system, the model doesn't issue a single prompt and wait for a response. It generates a plan of action, executes tool calls, compiles all the returned data, and culminates in completing an action or returning an answer to the user. The CPU is in charge of parsing that output, figuring out which tool to invoke, making the API calls or running the code, collecting the result, and feeding it back. Then the loop repeats—sometimes dozens of times per user request, with parallel sub-agents adding more CPU coordination work on top. The model quickly becomes one component of a larger reasoning loop. The ratio of organizational work to pure computation shifts, making the CPU a much bigger player, and potential bottleneck, in the full process.

In a collaboration between researchers at Georgia Tech and Intel, researchers found that in agentic workloads, CPU-side tool processing accounts for 50–90% of total end-to-end latency. Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, at Computex 2026, framed the shift precisely: "for reinforcement learning, orchestration, and agents, the CPU is a much better fit."

The numbers from Intel's Q1 2026 earnings call quantify how far this has already moved:

  • Training workloads: ~1 CPU per 8 GPUs
  • Inference workloads: Already shifted to ~1 CPU per 4 GPUs
  • Agentic workloads: Converging toward 1:1, with some customers reporting 4 CPUs deployed per GPU

Intel's Q1 2026 Data Center and AI segment revenue came in at $5.1B, up 22% year-over-year, with demand running ahead of supply. Intel has deprioritized consumer chip production to redirect fab capacity to server Xeon parts.

Arm's own analysis forecasts the shift more starkly. Traditional AI data centers require approximately 30 million CPU cores per gigawatt (GW) of capacity. Arm CEO Rene Haas estimates in the AI agent era, that figure rises to 120 million CPU cores per GW. The orchestration demands of agentic workloads drive this proposed 4× increase.

The second driver: Smaller, localized models

Separate from the shift agentic AI is cultivating, a second structural change is pushing inference toward CPUs. This change is the move toward smaller, domain-specific models deployed close to where data is generated.

We can attribute this change in tides to 4 main pressures on providers:

  1. Latency: A round-trip to a GPU cluster in a cloud data center takes time. For real-time applications like voice interfaces, autonomous systems, and industrial monitoring, that latency budget is measured in milliseconds. Local computing removes the network roundtrip.
  2. Privacy: Sending data off-device or off-premises to a cloud provider means data leaves the organization's control. Healthcare, finance, legal, and many other enterprise workflows increasingly cannot tolerate this. While this doesn't guarantee your data is being picked apart and auctioned off to the highest bidder or used for training, a local or CPU-resident model running on existing on-premises server infrastructure processes data without it ever leaving the facility, completely mitigating that risk.
  3. Cost: A single GPU can cost upwards of $45,000. For workloads that don't require the throughput of a GPU, that cost is unjustifiable. CPU inference on already-provisioned server infrastructure has a near-zero marginal hardware cost.
  4. Offline availability: Edge deployments frequently operate without reliable internet connectivity. Cloud GPU inference isn't an option in these scenarios. Local CPU inference is.

Small language models (SLMs) have matured to the point where this is viable. Hugging Face SmolLM2, ranging from 135M to 1.7B parameters, is designed for maximum efficiency on resource-constrained devices. The 135M variant fits entirely in CPU cache on modern smartphones. The performance gap between SLMs and large models narrows drastically when SLMs are augmented with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and reverses entirely on domain-specific tasks after fine-tuning.

A model trained on carefully curated data can achieve domain-specific performance with 100× less compute than training a general-purpose LLM. That's the caveat though. When it comes to fine-tuning and training models on larger GPUs, you have a lot more headroom to throw things at the model. On these smaller deployments, users need to be much more aware of the actions they're taking to produce performant and competitive models.

What this looks like in the industry today

These aren't theoretical workloads. The CPU era is fast approaching, if not already here.

OpenAI and AWS signed a $38B, 7-year infrastructure partnership in November 2025. The press release states access to hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs, with the ability to expand to tens of millions of CPUs to rapidly scale agentic workloads.

In March, Arm launched the AGI CPU, marking the company's first production silicon in its 35-year history. NVIDIA launched the Vera CPU at GTC San Jose in March 2026, calling it "the world's first processor purpose-built for agentic AI." Jensen Huang described it as NVIDIA's "next multibillion dollar business." The Vera CPU delivers:

  • 1.8× faster sandbox performance compared to leading x86 CPUs for agentic inner-loop work (code compilation, Python tool chains, software code analysis)
  • 2× memory bandwidth and 3× bandwidth per core compared to leading x86 CPUs with DDR5, via LPDDR5X memory with SOCAMM

First deliveries went to Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, who announced plans to deploy hundreds of thousands of Vera CPUs beginning in 2026.

NVIDIA's flagship agentic inference platform, the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, combines 72 Rubin GPUs with 36 Vera CPUs per rack, illustrating a pivot from the traditional 1:8 CPU:GPU ratio to a 1:2 ratio. The architecture is explicitly optimized to use GPUs for token generation and CPUs for everything wrapping it.

Morgan Stanley estimates the agentic CPU shift represents $32.5–$60B in incremental CPU market growth by 2030.

Figure 1: The industry shift toward CPU-heavy AI infrastructure, highlighting NVIDIA Vera CPU's 1.8× performance advantage, the NVL72 rack's 1:8 to 1:2 CPU-to-GPU ratio change, and key developments from Arm, OpenAI/AWS, and Morgan Stanley projecting $32.5–$60B in CPU market growth by 2030.

Measuring and deploying LLMs on CPUs

For GPU-dominated inference workloads, the GPU advantage is substantial and well-documented. A single H200 serving Llama 3.1 8B hits approximately 7,464 generation tokens/sec on chat workloads. The best-performing CPU virtual machine (VM) in the same Azure benchmark falls significantly short.

But peak throughput under high concurrency isn't the benchmark that matters most for CPU inference. It's more relevant to measure the workload profile corresponding to CPU-appropriate deployments, which can be more complicated to test properly.

GPU benchmarking has established norms, but CPU inference benchmarking is currently a mess of vendor-specific or not-so-reproducible numbers. The key difference is that CPUs share cores, memory bandwidth, and cache with everything else on the machine, so isolation requires careful socket-level or node-level separation GPU setups don't need. Red Hat's response is an open source 3-phase framework (vllm-cpu-perf-eval) using Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform and GuideLLM testing baseline capacity, realistic traffic variance, and production optimizations in a reproducible, standardized way.

This can all sound pretty daunting, especially if your mental model of LLM deployment is still built around GPU clusters. In practice, the ecosystem has matured considerably. Red Hat has a wide collection of validated models on Hugging Face. Additionally, Intel's AI Software Catalog lists a broad range of production-ready models validated and optimized for Xeon Gen 4–6 processors with vLLM support.

For a hands-on look at what deployment looks like, our recent vLLM office hours session walks through end-to-end inference deployment on Intel CPUs.

The architecture that makes CPU inference work

Several developments in the software stack have made CPU inference viable at a level it was not 2 years ago.

vLLM's CPU backend supports continuous batching, PagedAttention, prefix caching, chunked prefill, and tensor parallelism. These are the same scheduling and memory management primitives driving high-throughput GPU serving, but now also on:

  • x86 AVX-512
  • Arm AArch64
  • Apple Silicon (currently experimental)
  • IBM Z

The OpenAI-compatible API is identical across backends, which means a deployment starting on CPU infrastructure can migrate to GPU without application-layer changes.

On Arm, the oneDNN and Arm Compute Library build path, combined with INT4 quantization via llmcompressor, is a production path tested on AWS Graviton4.

On Intel, Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX) enables Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX)-backed BF16 operations automatically when installed. The key environment variables give operators direct control over the memory and threading tradeoffs that matter most for CPU serving:

  • VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE(KV cache allocation in GB)
  • VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND(OpenMP thread pinning)
  • The experimental VLLM_CPU_SGL_KERNEL (AMX + BF16 small-batch kernels)

Conclusion

The GPU isn't going anywhere. For high-concurrency production serving of large models, GPU is the right answer and will remain so.

What's changed is the perimeter of that statement. Agentic AI introduced a class of workloads—orchestration, tool execution, code sandboxing, and multi-agent coordination—where CPUs are the correct tool for the job. The ratio shift from 1:8 to 1:1 in Intel's data center projections isn't a temporary anomaly. This momentous change is the consequence of inference becoming iterative rather than single-shot.

At the same time, the economics and constraints of edge deployment—latency, privacy, cost, and offline availability—drive a parallel wave of CPU-based inference for small, localized models where GPU infrastructure was never the right fit.

NVIDIA building Vera. Arm jumping back into the game. Intel's Xeon demand running ahead of supply. OpenAI contracting for tens of millions of CPUs. The CPU is back.

What next?

  • Deploy models on CPUs with vLLM on OpenShift AI: Red Hat is a leading contributor to vLLM, and Red Hat OpenShift AI provides a supported, production-grade platform for serving models on both CPU and GPU infrastructure, with the same OpenAI-compatible API regardless of backend.
  • Benchmark your CPU inference performance: Use the open source vllm-cpu-perf-eval framework, along with GuideLLM, to establish reproducible baselines for your hardware and workloads.

blocks.html_en: For the past 3 years, graphics processing units (GPUs) have dominated the large language model (LLM) conversation. In traditional chatbot applications, central processing units (CPUs) provide a fraction of the total compute per request, while GPUs do the heavy lifting. However, inference isn't a single model answering a single question. A growing reliance on tool calls, multistep reasoning, and orchestration across small, specialized models changes the math on where compute should live. Intel has called out this shift noting that the CPU-to-GPU ratio is moving from 1:8 in training workloads to 1:1, and in some cases 4:1 in agentic deployments.

sentences.en: In traditional chatbot applications, central processing units (CPUs) provide a fraction of the total compute per request, while GPUs do the heavy lifting.
sentences.zh: 在传统的聊天机器人应用程序中，中央处理单元 (CPU) 提供每个请求总计算量的一小部分，而 GPU 则承担繁重的工作。

sentences.en: However, inference isn't a single model answering a single question.

blocks.html_en: Here we'll examine why the assumptions making GPUs the obvious choice for LLM inference are being renegotiated, what's driving renewed demand for CPU-based serving, and what the data says about where the industry is heading.

sentences.en: Here we'll examine why the assumptions making GPUs the obvious choice for LLM inference are being renegotiated, what's driving renewed demand for CPU-based serving, and what the data says about where the industry is heading.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们将研究为什么 GPU 成为 LLM 推理的明显选择的假设正在重新协商，是什么推动了对基于 CPU 的服务的新需求，以及数据表明了该行业的发展方向。

blocks.html_en: What CPUs are good at

sentences.en: What CPUs are good at
sentences.zh: CPU 擅长什么

blocks.html_en: At their core (no pun intended), CPUs and GPUs solve fundamentally different problems.

sentences.en: At their core (no pun intended), CPUs and GPUs solve fundamentally different problems.
sentences.zh: CPU 和 GPU 的核心（无双关语）解决的是根本不同的问题。

blocks.html_en: A modern GPU contains tens of thousands of cores designed to execute the same operation on thousands of data elements simultaneously. This makes them extraordinarily fast at the dense matrix multiplications that dominate the forward pass of a transformer for inference. During training, and during high-concurrency batched inference, that parallelism translates directly into throughput: greater tokens per second (TPS), and many more requests served per dollar of compute.

sentences.en: A modern GPU contains tens of thousands of cores designed to execute the same operation on thousands of data elements simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 现代 GPU 包含数万个内核，旨在同时对数千个数据元素执行相同的操作。

sentences.en: This makes them extraordinarily fast at the dense matrix multiplications that dominate the forward pass of a transformer for inference.
sentences.zh: 这使得它们在密集矩阵乘法方面异常快速，而密集矩阵乘法在推理变压器的前向传递中占主导地位。

sentences.en: During training, and during high-concurrency batched inference, that parallelism translates directly into throughput: greater tokens per second (TPS), and many more requests served per dollar of compute.
sentences.zh: 在训练期间和高并发批量推理期间，并行性直接转化为吞吐量：每秒处理更多的令牌 (TPS)，以及每美元计算服务的请求数量更多。

blocks.html_en: Modern CPUs, by contrast, have anywhere from one to hundreds of cores optimized for sequential, conditional, and branching logic. They're particularly fast at a single operation moving through a complex decision tree. They have direct access to main system memory, and they're the natural execution environment for the orchestration layer wrapping any model. Tool dispatch, code execution, Python runtimes, sandboxes, input/output (I/O), and the agent loop control flow all sit in the CPU.

sentences.en: Modern CPUs, by contrast, have anywhere from one to hundreds of cores optimized for sequential, conditional, and branching logic.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，现代 CPU 拥有从一到数百个针对顺序逻辑、条件逻辑和分支逻辑进行优化的内核。

sentences.en: They're particularly fast at a single operation moving through a complex decision tree.
sentences.zh: 它们在复杂决策树中的单个操作中速度特别快。

sentences.en: They have direct access to main system memory, and they're the natural execution environment for the orchestration layer wrapping any model.
sentences.zh: 它们可以直接访问主系统内存，并且它们是包装任何模型的编排层的自然执行环境。

sentences.en: Tool dispatch, code execution, Python runtimes, sandboxes, input/output (I/O), and the agent loop control flow all sit in the CPU.
sentences.zh: 工具调度、代码执行、Python 运行时、沙箱、输入/输出 (I/O) 和代理循环控制流都位于 CPU 中。

blocks.html_en: These architectures, while different in nature, aren't competitors; they work best in tandem. The real question isn't which architecture is better, but which workload belongs where.

sentences.en: These architectures, while different in nature, aren't competitors; they work best in tandem.
sentences.zh: 这些架构虽然本质上不同，但并不是竞争对手；而是不同的。它们协同工作效果最佳。

sentences.en: The real question isn't which architecture is better, but which workload belongs where.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题不在于哪种架构更好，而在于哪种工作负载属于哪里。

blocks.html_en: This division of labor comes down to how we measure their work: FLOPS versus instruction latency.

sentences.en: This division of labor comes down to how we measure their work: FLOPS versus instruction latency.
sentences.zh: 这种分工取决于我们如何衡量他们的工作：FLOPS 与指令延迟。

blocks.html_en: GPUs live and die by floating-point operations per second (FLOPS). Because AI models are massive webs of decimal numbers being multiplied and added, a GPU's job is to brute-force trillions of these matrix calculations simultaneously. It's built entirely for raw mathematical throughput.

sentences.en: GPUs live and die by floating-point operations per second (FLOPS).
sentences.zh: GPU 的生死取决于每秒浮点运算次数 (FLOPS)。

sentences.en: Because AI models are massive webs of decimal numbers being multiplied and added, a GPU's job is to brute-force trillions of these matrix calculations simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 由于 AI 模型是由十进制数字相乘和相加组成的巨大网络，因此 GPU 的工作就是同时强力执行数万亿个矩阵计算。

sentences.en: It's built entirely for raw mathematical throughput.
sentences.zh: 它完全是为了原始数学吞吐量而构建的。

blocks.html_en: CPUs, by contrast, specialize in instruction latency. Instruction latency measures how fast a single core can execute an unpredictable chain of diverse commands. A CPU core excels at the rapid logic shuffling needed to parse JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), handle network I/O, or check security permissions.

sentences.en: CPUs, by contrast, specialize in instruction latency.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，CPU 专注于指令延迟。

sentences.en: Instruction latency measures how fast a single core can execute an unpredictable chain of diverse commands.
sentences.zh: 指令延迟衡量单个内核执行不可预测的不同命令链的速度。

sentences.en: A CPU core excels at the rapid logic shuffling needed to parse JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), handle network I/O, or check security permissions.
sentences.zh: CPU 内核擅长解析 JavaScript 对象表示法 (JSON)、处理网络 I/O 或检查安全权限所需的快速逻辑改组。

blocks.html_en: If you force a GPU to run a chaotic Python runtime, its massive FLOP capacity sits idle, choked by constant task-switching. If you force a CPU to crunch an LLM's math, it works perfectly, but takes ages because it lacks the massive parallel pipelines. The GPU is the mathematical muscle; the CPU is the logic engine directing the show.

sentences.en: If you force a GPU to run a chaotic Python runtime, its massive FLOP capacity sits idle, choked by constant task-switching.
sentences.zh: 如果你强迫 GPU 运行混乱的 Python 运行时，其巨大的 FLOP 能力就会闲置，并被不断的任务切换所阻塞。

sentences.en: If you force a CPU to crunch an LLM's math, it works perfectly, but takes ages because it lacks the massive parallel pipelines.
sentences.zh: 如果你强迫CPU来处理LLM的数学，它可以完美地工作，但需要很长时间，因为它缺乏大规模的并行管道。

sentences.en: The GPU is the mathematical muscle; the CPU is the logic engine directing the show.
sentences.zh: GPU 是数学肌肉； CPU是指挥表演的逻辑引擎。

blocks.html_en: The traditional inference stack: Where CPUs were passengers

sentences.en: The traditional inference stack: Where CPUs were passengers
sentences.zh: 传统推理堆栈：CPU 是乘客

blocks.html_en: When we think of the traditional inference stack, we think about the chatbot serving application. Here, the CPU often plays a supporting role.

sentences.en: When we think of the traditional inference stack, we think about the chatbot serving application.
sentences.zh: 当我们想到传统的推理堆栈时，我们会想到聊天机器人服务应用程序。

sentences.en: Here, the CPU often plays a supporting role.
sentences.zh: 在这里，CPU往往扮演着配角的角色。

blocks.html_en: A request arrives at the API server, where the CPU tokenizes and schedules it. The CPU handles all these initial tasks. It then hands the request to the GPU for the forward pass, which dominates the compute budget. The GPU runs attention, feeds forward layers, and samples the next token with a brief CPU sync to retrieve it and update the scheduler. It then repeats until an end-of-sequence token is emitted. Finally, the CPU collects the output and returns it to end the session.

sentences.en: A request arrives at the API server, where the CPU tokenizes and schedules it.
sentences.zh: 请求到达 API 服务器，CPU 在其中对其进行标记和调度。

sentences.en: The CPU handles all these initial tasks.
sentences.zh: CPU 处理所有这些初始任务。

sentences.en: It then hands the request to the GPU for the forward pass, which dominates the compute budget.
sentences.zh: 然后，它将请求交给 GPU 进行前向传递，这在计算预算中占主导地位。

sentences.en: The GPU runs attention, feeds forward layers, and samples the next token with a brief CPU sync to retrieve it and update the scheduler.
sentences.zh: GPU 运行注意力、前馈层，并通过简短的 CPU 同步对下一个令牌进行采样，以检索它并更新调度程序。

sentences.en: It then repeats until an end-of-sequence token is emitted.
sentences.zh: 然后重复直到发出序列结束标记。

sentences.en: Finally, the CPU collects the output and returns it to end the session.
sentences.zh: 最后，CPU 收集输出并将其返回以结束会话。

blocks.html_en: In this model, the CPU acts as a receptionist, doing the coordination and organizational work, while the GPU does the computational heavy lifting. The ratio of CPUs to GPUs in AI data centers during the training era reflected this: roughly 1 to 2 CPUs for every 8 GPUs, a ratio dictated more by GPUs throughput than by CPU demand. Teams provisioned CPUs to keep GPUs fed. This setup is slowly shifting away from the de facto standard, as advancements in CPU inference increase global efficiency.

sentences.en: In this model, the CPU acts as a receptionist, doing the coordination and organizational work, while the GPU does the computational heavy lifting.
sentences.zh: 在此模型中，CPU 充当接待员，负责协调和组织工作，而 GPU 负责计算繁重的工作。

sentences.en: The ratio of CPUs to GPUs in AI data centers during the training era reflected this: roughly 1 to 2 CPUs for every 8 GPUs, a ratio dictated more by GPUs throughput than by CPU demand.
sentences.zh: 训练期间人工智能数据中心的 CPU 与 GPU 的比例反映了这一点：大约每 8 个 GPU 对应 1 到 2 个 CPU，这一比例更多地由 GPU 吞吐量决定，而不是由 CPU 需求决定。

sentences.en: Teams provisioned CPUs to keep GPUs fed.
sentences.zh: 团队配置 CPU 来满足 GPU 的需求。

sentences.en: This setup is slowly shifting away from the de facto standard, as advancements in CPU inference increase global efficiency.
sentences.zh: 随着 CPU 推理的进步提高了全局效率，这种设置正在慢慢偏离事实上的标准。

blocks.html_en: The first driver: How agents are changing the workload

sentences.en: The first driver: How agents are changing the workload
sentences.zh: 第一个驱动因素：客服人员如何改变工作量

blocks.html_en: With the rise of agentic AI comes a new inference profile magnifying the need for CPU-specific compute.

sentences.en: With the rise of agentic AI comes a new inference profile magnifying the need for CPU-specific compute.
sentences.zh: 随着代理人工智能的兴起，新的推理配置文件放大了对特定于 CPU 的计算的需求。

blocks.html_en: "Agentic AI" conjures up images of integrated agent harnesses, like Hermes and Openclaw, and developers with hosts of agents tied into their coding assistants. While these use cases are becoming more popular, agentic AI isn't as niche as it may seem at first glance. In fact, many people aren't using the "traditional" process of querying a chatbot. Popular AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT are backed by enormous models that often incorporate "reasoning" stages into their more complex responses. During reasoning, the "chatbot" becomes a full agentic system. A single user-visible task may decompose into dozens of individual model calls, each of which is short, context-dependent, and conditionally branching.

sentences.en: "Agentic AI" conjures up images of integrated agent harnesses, like Hermes and Openclaw, and developers with hosts of agents tied into their coding assistants.
sentences.zh: “Agent AI”让人联想到集成代理工具的图像，例如 Hermes 和 Openclaw，以及将大量代理与编码助手绑定在一起的开发人员。

sentences.en: While these use cases are becoming more popular, agentic AI isn't as niche as it may seem at first glance.
sentences.zh: 虽然这些用例变得越来越流行，但代理人工智能并不像乍一看那样小众。

sentences.en: In fact, many people aren't using the "traditional" process of querying a chatbot.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多人没有使用查询聊天机器人的“传统”流程。

sentences.en: Popular AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT are backed by enormous models that often incorporate "reasoning" stages into their more complex responses.
sentences.zh: Claude 和 ChatGPT 等流行的人工智能助手得到了巨大模型的支持，这些模型通常将“推理”阶段融入到更复杂的响应中。

sentences.en: During reasoning, the "chatbot" becomes a full agentic system.
sentences.zh: 在推理过程中，“聊天机器人”变成了一个完整的代理系统。

sentences.en: A single user-visible task may decompose into dozens of individual model calls, each of which is short, context-dependent, and conditionally branching.
sentences.zh: 单个用户可见的任务可以分解为数十个单独的模型调用，每个模型调用都很短、依赖于上下文并且有条件分支。

blocks.html_en: In an agentic system, the model doesn't issue a single prompt and wait for a response. It generates a plan of action, executes tool calls, compiles all the returned data, and culminates in completing an action or returning an answer to the user. The CPU is in charge of parsing that output, figuring out which tool to invoke, making the API calls or running the code, collecting the result, and feeding it back. Then the loop repeats—sometimes dozens of times per user request, with parallel sub-agents adding more CPU coordination work on top. The model quickly becomes one component of a larger reasoning loop. The ratio of organizational work to pure computation shifts, making the CPU a much bigger player, and potential bottleneck, in the full process.

sentences.en: In an agentic system, the model doesn't issue a single prompt and wait for a response.
sentences.zh: 在代理系统中，模型不会发出单个提示并等待响应。

sentences.en: It generates a plan of action, executes tool calls, compiles all the returned data, and culminates in completing an action or returning an answer to the user.
sentences.zh: 它生成行动计划，执行工具调用，编译所有返回的数据，并最终完成操作或向用户返回答案。

sentences.en: The CPU is in charge of parsing that output, figuring out which tool to invoke, making the API calls or running the code, collecting the result, and feeding it back.
sentences.zh: CPU 负责解析该输出、确定要调用哪个工具、进行 API 调用或运行代码、收集结果并将其反馈回来。

sentences.en: Then the loop repeats—sometimes dozens of times per user request, with parallel sub-agents adding more CPU coordination work on top.
sentences.zh: 然后循环重复，有时每个用户请求重复数十次，并行子代理在顶部添加更多的 CPU 协调工作。

sentences.en: The model quickly becomes one component of a larger reasoning loop.
sentences.zh: 该模型很快就会成为更大的推理循环的一个组成部分。

sentences.en: The ratio of organizational work to pure computation shifts, making the CPU a much bigger player, and potential bottleneck, in the full process.
sentences.zh: 组织工作与纯计算的比例发生了变化，使得 CPU 在整个过程中扮演了更大的角色，并成为潜在的瓶颈。

blocks.html_en: In a collaboration between researchers at Georgia Tech and Intel, researchers found that in agentic workloads, CPU-side tool processing accounts for 50–90% of total end-to-end latency. Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, at Computex 2026, framed the shift precisely: "for reinforcement learning, orchestration, and agents, the CPU is a much better fit."

sentences.en: In a collaboration between researchers at Georgia Tech and Intel, researchers found that in agentic workloads, CPU-side tool processing accounts for 50–90% of total end-to-end latency.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚理工学院和英特尔的研究人员合作中，研究人员发现，在代理工作负载中，CPU 端工具处理占端到端总延迟的 50-90%。

sentences.en: Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, at Computex 2026, framed the shift precisely: "for reinforcement learning, orchestration, and agents, the CPU is a much better fit."
sentences.zh: 英特尔首席执行官 Lip-Bu Tan 在 Computex 2026 上精确地阐述了这一转变：“对于强化学习、编排和代理来说，CPU 更适合。”

sentences.zh: 训练工作负载：每 8 个 GPU 约 1 个 CPU

sentences.zh: 代理工作负载：趋向于 1:1，一些客户报告每个 GPU 部署了 4 个 CPU

sentences.en: Intel's Q1 2026 Data Center and AI segment revenue came in at $5.1B, up 22% year-over-year, with demand running ahead of supply.
sentences.zh: 英特尔 2026 年第一季度数据中心和人工智能部门收入为 $5.1B，同比增长 22%，需求超过供应。

sentences.en: Arm's own analysis forecasts the shift more starkly.

sentences.en: Traditional AI data centers require approximately 30 million CPU cores per gigawatt (GW) of capacity.

sentences.en: The second driver: Smaller, localized models

blocks.html_en: Separate from the shift agentic AI is cultivating, a second structural change is pushing inference toward CPUs. This change is the move toward smaller, domain-specific models deployed close to where data is generated.

sentences.en: Separate from the shift agentic AI is cultivating, a second structural change is pushing inference toward CPUs.
sentences.zh: 除了智能人工智能正在培育的转变之外，第二个结构性变化正在将推理推向 CPU。

sentences.en: This change is the move toward smaller, domain-specific models deployed close to where data is generated.
sentences.zh: 这一变化是朝着部署在数据生成位置附近的更小的、特定于领域的模型的方向发展。

blocks.html_en: We can attribute this change in tides to 4 main pressures on providers:

sentences.en: We can attribute this change in tides to 4 main pressures on providers:
sentences.zh: 我们可以将这种潮汐变化归因于供应商面临的 4 个主要压力：

blocks.html_en: • Latency: A round-trip to a GPU cluster in a cloud data center takes time. For real-time applications like voice interfaces, autonomous systems, and industrial monitoring, that latency budget is measured in milliseconds. Local computing removes the network roundtrip.

sentences.en: Latency: A round-trip to a GPU cluster in a cloud data center takes time.
sentences.zh: 延迟：到云数据中心的 GPU 集群的往返需要时间。

sentences.en: For real-time applications like voice interfaces, autonomous systems, and industrial monitoring, that latency budget is measured in milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 对于语音接口、自治系统和工业监控等实时应用，延迟预算以毫秒为单位。

sentences.en: Local computing removes the network roundtrip.
sentences.zh: 本地计算消除了网络往返。

blocks.html_en: • Privacy: Sending data off-device or off-premises to a cloud provider means data leaves the organization's control. While this doesn't guarantee your data is being picked apart and auctioned off to the highest bidder or used for training, a local or CPU-resident model running on existing on-premises server infrastructure processes data without it ever leaving the facility, completely mitigating that risk.

sentences.en: Privacy: Sending data off-device or off-premises to a cloud provider means data leaves the organization's control.
sentences.zh: 隐私：将数据从设备或外部发送到云提供商意味着数据脱离了组织的控制。

sentences.en: Healthcare, finance, legal, and many other enterprise workflows increasingly cannot tolerate this.

sentences.en: While this doesn't guarantee your data is being picked apart and auctioned off to the highest bidder or used for training, a local or CPU-resident model running on existing on-premises server infrastructure processes data without it ever leaving the facility, completely mitigating that risk.
sentences.zh: 虽然这并不能保证您的数据被拆开并拍卖给最高出价者或用于培训，但在现有本地服务器基础设施上运行的本地或 CPU 驻留模型可以在数据不离开设施的情况下处理数据，从而完全降低了风险。

blocks.html_en: • Cost: A single GPU can cost upwards of $45,000. For workloads that don't require the throughput of a GPU, that cost is unjustifiable. CPU inference on already-provisioned server infrastructure has a near-zero marginal hardware cost.

sentences.en: Cost: A single GPU can cost upwards of $45,000.

sentences.en: Small language models (SLMs) have matured to the point where this is viable.

blocks.html_en: For GPU-dominated inference workloads, the GPU advantage is substantial and well-documented. A single H200 serving Llama 3.1 8B hits approximately 7,464 generation tokens/sec on chat workloads. The best-performing CPU virtual machine (VM) in the same Azure benchmark falls significantly short.

sentences.en: For GPU-dominated inference workloads, the GPU advantage is substantial and well-documented.
sentences.zh: 对于 GPU 主导的推理工作负载，GPU 的优势是巨大且有据可查的。

sentences.en: A single H200 serving Llama 3.1 8B hits approximately 7,464 generation tokens/sec on chat workloads.
sentences.zh: 为 Llama 3.1 8B 提供服务的单个 H200 在聊天工作负载上达到每秒约 7,464 个生成令牌。

sentences.en: The best-performing CPU virtual machine (VM) in the same Azure benchmark falls significantly short.
sentences.zh: 在同一 Azure 基准测试中，性能最佳的 CPU 虚拟机 (VM) 明显落后。

blocks.html_en: But peak throughput under high concurrency isn't the benchmark that matters most for CPU inference. It's more relevant to measure the workload profile corresponding to CPU-appropriate deployments, which can be more complicated to test properly.

sentences.zh: 更重要的是测量与适合 CPU 的部署相对应的工作负载配置文件，正确测试可能会更复杂。

blocks.html_en: GPU benchmarking has established norms, but CPU inference benchmarking is currently a mess of vendor-specific or not-so-reproducible numbers. The key difference is that CPUs share cores, memory bandwidth, and cache with everything else on the machine, so isolation requires careful socket-level or node-level separation GPU setups don't need. Red Hat's response is an open source 3-phase framework (vllm-cpu-perf-eval) using Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform and GuideLLM testing baseline capacity, realistic traffic variance, and production optimizations in a reproducible, standardized way.

sentences.en: GPU benchmarking has established norms, but CPU inference benchmarking is currently a mess of vendor-specific or not-so-reproducible numbers.

sentences.zh: 红帽的回应是开源三阶段框架 (vllm-cpu-perf-eval)，使用红帽 Ansible 自动化平台和 GuideLLM 以可重复的标准化方式测试基线容量、实际流量差异和生产优化。

blocks.html_en: The GPU isn't going anywhere. For high-concurrency production serving of large models, GPU is the right answer and will remain so.

sentences.en: The GPU isn't going anywhere.
sentences.zh: GPU 不会去任何地方。

sentences.en: For high-concurrency production serving of large models, GPU is the right answer and will remain so.
sentences.zh: 对于大型模型的高并发生产服务，GPU 是正确的答案，并且将继续如此。

blocks.html_en: What's changed is the perimeter of that statement. Agentic AI introduced a class of workloads—orchestration, tool execution, code sandboxing, and multi-agent coordination—where CPUs are the correct tool for the job. The ratio shift from 1:8 to 1:1 in Intel's data center projections isn't a temporary anomaly. This momentous change is the consequence of inference becoming iterative rather than single-shot.

sentences.en: What's changed is the perimeter of that statement.
sentences.zh: 改变的是该语句的范围。

sentences.en: Agentic AI introduced a class of workloads—orchestration, tool execution, code sandboxing, and multi-agent coordination—where CPUs are the correct tool for the job.

sentences.en: The ratio shift from 1:8 to 1:1 in Intel's data center projections isn't a temporary anomaly.
sentences.zh: 英特尔数据中心预测中的比率从 1:8 变为 1:1 并不是暂时的异常现象。

sentences.en: This momentous change is the consequence of inference becoming iterative rather than single-shot.
sentences.zh: 这一重大变化是推理变得迭代而不是单次的结果。

blocks.html_en: At the same time, the economics and constraints of edge deployment—latency, privacy, cost, and offline availability—drive a parallel wave of CPU-based inference for small, localized models where GPU infrastructure was never the right fit.

开发者倡导者

在过去的 3 年里，图形处理单元 (GPU) 一直主导着大型语言模型 (LLM) 的讨论。 在传统的聊天机器人应用程序中，中央处理单元 (CPU) 提供每个请求总计算量的一小部分，而 GPU 则承担繁重的工作。 然而，推理并不是回答单一问题的单一模型。 对工具调用、多步推理和跨小型专用模型的编排的日益依赖改变了计算应该存在的数学方式。 英特尔指出了这一转变，并指出 CPU 与 GPU 的比例正在从训练工作负载中的 1:8 变为 1:1，在某些情况下，在代理部署中甚至变为 4:1。

在这里，我们将研究为什么 GPU 成为 LLM 推理的明显选择的假设正在重新协商，是什么推动了对基于 CPU 的服务的新需求，以及数据表明了该行业的发展方向。

CPU 擅长什么

CPU 和 GPU 的核心（无双关语）解决的是根本不同的问题。

现代 GPU 包含数万个内核，旨在同时对数千个数据元素执行相同的操作。 这使得它们在密集矩阵乘法方面异常快速，而密集矩阵乘法在推理变压器的前向传递中占主导地位。 在训练期间和高并发批量推理期间，并行性直接转化为吞吐量：每秒处理更多的令牌 (TPS)，以及每美元计算服务的请求数量更多。

相比之下，现代 CPU 拥有从一到数百个针对顺序逻辑、条件逻辑和分支逻辑进行优化的内核。 它们在复杂决策树中的单个操作中速度特别快。 它们可以直接访问主系统内存，并且它们是包装任何模型的编排层的自然执行环境。 工具调度、代码执行、Python 运行时、沙箱、输入/输出 (I/O) 和代理循环控制流都位于 CPU 中。

这些架构虽然本质上不同，但并不是竞争对手；而是不同的。它们协同工作效果最佳。 真正的问题不在于哪种架构更好，而在于哪种工作负载属于哪里。

这种分工取决于我们如何衡量他们的工作：FLOPS 与指令延迟。

GPU 的生死取决于每秒浮点运算次数 (FLOPS)。 由于 AI 模型是由十进制数字相乘和相加组成的巨大网络，因此 GPU 的工作就是同时强力执行数万亿个矩阵计算。 它完全是为了原始数学吞吐量而构建的。

相比之下，CPU 专注于指令延迟。 指令延迟衡量单个内核执行不可预测的不同命令链的速度。 CPU 内核擅长解析 JavaScript 对象表示法 (JSON)、处理网络 I/O 或检查安全权限所需的快速逻辑改组。

如果你强迫 GPU 运行混乱的 Python 运行时，其巨大的 FLOP 能力就会闲置，并被不断的任务切换所阻塞。 如果你强迫CPU来处理LLM的数学，它可以完美地工作，但需要很长时间，因为它缺乏大规模的并行管道。 GPU 是数学肌肉； CPU是指挥表演的逻辑引擎。

传统推理堆栈：CPU 是乘客

当我们想到传统的推理堆栈时，我们会想到聊天机器人服务应用程序。 在这里，CPU往往扮演着配角的角色。

请求到达 API 服务器，CPU 在其中对其进行标记和调度。 CPU 处理所有这些初始任务。 然后，它将请求交给 GPU 进行前向传递，这在计算预算中占主导地位。 GPU 运行注意力、前馈层，并通过简短的 CPU 同步对下一个令牌进行采样，以检索它并更新调度程序。 然后重复直到发出序列结束标记。 最后，CPU 收集输出并将其返回以结束会话。

在此模型中，CPU 充当接待员，负责协调和组织工作，而 GPU 负责计算繁重的工作。 训练期间人工智能数据中心的 CPU 与 GPU 的比例反映了这一点：大约每 8 个 GPU 对应 1 到 2 个 CPU，这一比例更多地由 GPU 吞吐量决定，而不是由 CPU 需求决定。 团队配置 CPU 来满足 GPU 的需求。 随着 CPU 推理的进步提高了全局效率，这种设置正在慢慢偏离事实上的标准。

第一个驱动因素：客服人员如何改变工作量

随着代理人工智能的兴起，新的推理配置文件放大了对特定于 CPU 的计算的需求。

“Agent AI”让人联想到集成代理工具的图像，例如 Hermes 和 Openclaw，以及将大量代理与编码助手绑定在一起的开发人员。 虽然这些用例变得越来越流行，但代理人工智能并不像乍一看那样小众。 事实上，许多人没有使用查询聊天机器人的“传统”流程。 Claude 和 ChatGPT 等流行的人工智能助手得到了巨大模型的支持，这些模型通常将“推理”阶段融入到更复杂的响应中。 在推理过程中，“聊天机器人”变成了一个完整的代理系统。 单个用户可见的任务可以分解为数十个单独的模型调用，每个模型调用都很短、依赖于上下文并且有条件分支。

在代理系统中，模型不会发出单个提示并等待响应。 它生成行动计划，执行工具调用，编译所有返回的数据，并最终完成操作或向用户返回答案。 CPU 负责解析该输出、确定要调用哪个工具、进行 API 调用或运行代码、收集结果并将其反馈回来。 然后循环重复，有时每个用户请求重复数十次，并行子代理在顶部添加更多的 CPU 协调工作。 该模型很快就会成为更大的推理循环的一个组成部分。 组织工作与纯计算的比例发生了变化，使得 CPU 在整个过程中扮演了更大的角色，并成为潜在的瓶颈。

在佐治亚理工学院和英特尔的研究人员合作中，研究人员发现，在代理工作负载中，CPU 端工具处理占端到端总延迟的 50-90%。 英特尔首席执行官 Lip-Bu Tan 在 Computex 2026 上精确地阐述了这一转变：“对于强化学习、编排和代理来说，CPU 更适合。”

英特尔 2026 年第一季度财报电话会议的数据量化了这一趋势已经取得的进展：

  • 训练工作负载：每 8 个 GPU 约 1 个 CPU
  • 推理工作负载：已转变为每 4 个 GPU 约 1 个 CPU
  • 代理工作负载：趋向于 1:1，一些客户报告每个 GPU 部署了 4 个 CPU

英特尔 2026 年第一季度数据中心和人工智能部门收入为 $5.1B，同比增长 22%，需求超过供应。 英特尔已取消消费芯片生产的优先顺序，将晶圆厂产能转向服务器至强部件。

Arm 自己的分析预测这种转变更加明显。 传统 AI 数据中心每千兆瓦 (GW) 容量需要大约 3000 万个 CPU 内核。 Arm 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 估计，在人工智能代理时代，这一数字将上升至每 GW 1.2 亿个 CPU 核心。 代理工作负载的编排需求推动了拟议的 4 倍增长。

第二个驱动因素：更小的、本地化的车型

除了智能人工智能正在培育的转变之外，第二个结构性变化正在将推理推向 CPU。 这一变化是朝着部署在数据生成位置附近的更小的、特定于领域的模型的方向发展。

我们可以将这种潮汐变化归因于供应商面临的 4 个主要压力：

  1. 延迟：到云数据中心的 GPU 集群的往返需要时间。 对于语音接口、自治系统和工业监控等实时应用，延迟预算以毫秒为单位。 本地计算消除了网络往返。
  2. 隐私：将数据从设备或外部发送到云提供商意味着数据脱离了组织的控制。 医疗保健、金融、法律和许多其他企业工作流程越来越不能容忍这种情况。 虽然这并不能保证您的数据被拆开并拍卖给最高出价者或用于培训，但在现有本地服务器基础设施上运行的本地或 CPU 驻留模型可以在数据不离开设施的情况下处理数据，从而完全降低了风险。
  3. 成本：单个 GPU 的成本可能高达 45,000 美元。 对于不需要 GPU 吞吐量的工作负载，这种成本是不合理的。 在已配置的服务器基础设施上进行 CPU 推理的边际硬件成本接近于零。
  4. 离线可用性：边缘部署经常在没有可靠互联网连接的情况下运行。 在这些场景中，云 GPU 推理不是一个选项。 本地CPU推理是。

小语言模型 (SLM) 已经成熟到可以实现的程度。 Hugging Face SmolLM2 参数范围从 135M 到 1.7B，专为在资源受限的设备上实现最大效率而设计。 135M 版本完全适合现代智能手机的 CPU 缓存。 当 SLM 通过检索增强生成 (RAG) 进行增强时，SLM 和大型模型之间的性能差距会急剧缩小，并且在微调后在特定于领域的任务上完全逆转。

在精心策划的数据上训练的模型可以比训练通用 LLM 少 100 倍的计算量来实现特定领域的性能。 不过，这就是警告。 当涉及到在更大的 GPU 上微调和训练模型时，您有更多的空间来向模型扔东西。 在这些较小的部署中，用户需要更加了解他们为生成高性能和有竞争力的模型而采取的操作。

这在当今的行业中是什么样子的

这些不是理论上的工作负载。 CPU 时代即使还没有到来，也正在快速到来。

OpenAI 和 AWS 于 2025 年 11 月签署了价值 38B 美元、为期 7 年的基础设施合作伙伴关系。 该新闻稿称，可以使用数十万个 NVIDIA GPU，并能够扩展到数千万个 CPU，以快速扩展代理工作负载。

今年 3 月，Arm 推出了 AGI CPU，标志着该公司 35 年历史上首款量产芯片。 NVIDIA 于 2026 年 3 月在圣何塞 GTC 上推出了 Vera CPU，称其为“世界上首款专为代理 AI 打造的处理器”。 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 将其描述为 NVIDIA 的“下一个数十亿美元业务”。 Vera CPU 提供：

  • 与领先的 x86 CPU 相比，沙箱性能提高 1.8 倍，用于代理内循环工作（代码编译、Python 工具链、软件代码分析）
  • 与采用 DDR5 的领先 x86 CPU 相比，通过采用 SOCAMM 的 LPDDR5X 内存可实现 2 倍内存带宽和 3 倍每核带宽

第一批交付给了 Anthropic、OpenAI、SpaceXAI 和 Oracle Cloud Infrastructure，它们宣布计划从 2026 年开始部署数十万个 Vera CPU。

NVIDIA 的旗舰代理推理平台 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架将 72 个 Rubin GPU 与每个机架 36 个 Vera CPU 结合在一起，体现了从传统 1:8 CPU:GPU 比例到 1:2 比例的转变。 该架构经过明确优化，可使用 GPU 生成令牌，并使用 CPU 处理其包装的所有内容。

摩根士丹利估计，到 2030 年，CPU 的代理转移将导致 CPU 市场增量增长 $32.5–$60B。

在 CPU 上测量和部署 LLM

对于 GPU 主导的推理工作负载，GPU 的优势是巨大且有据可查的。 为 Llama 3.1 8B 提供服务的单个 H200 在聊天工作负载上达到每秒约 7,464 个生成令牌。 在同一 Azure 基准测试中，性能最佳的 CPU 虚拟机 (VM) 明显落后。

但高并发下的峰值吞吐量并不是 CPU 推理最重要的基准。 更重要的是测量与适合 CPU 的部署相对应的工作负载配置文件，正确测试可能会更复杂。

GPU 基准测试已经建立了规范，但 CPU 推理基准测试目前是一堆特定于供应商或不太可重复的数字。 关键区别在于 CPU 与计算机上的其他所有组件共享核心、内存带宽和缓存，因此隔离需要仔细的套接字级或节点级分离，而 GPU 设置则不需要。 红帽的回应是开源三阶段框架 (vllm-cpu-perf-eval)，使用红帽 Ansible 自动化平台和 GuideLLM 以可重复的标准化方式测试基线容量、实际流量差异和生产优化。

这听起来相当令人畏惧，尤其是如果您的 LLM 部署心智模型仍然围绕 GPU 集群构建的话。 实际上，生态系统已经相当成熟。 红帽在 Hugging Face 上拥有大量经过验证的模型。 此外，英特尔的 AI 软件目录还列出了一系列针对支持 vLLM 的 Xeon Gen 4-6 处理器进行验证和优化的生产就绪模型。

为了亲自了解部署是什么样子，我们最近的 vLLM 办公时间会议将介绍英特尔 CPU 上的端到端推理部署。

使 CPU 推理工作的架构

软件堆栈的多项发展使 CPU 推理的可行性达到了 2 年前的水平。

vLLM 的 CPU 后端支持连续批处理、PagedAttention、前缀缓存、分块预填充和张量并行。 这些是驱动高吞吐量 GPU 服务的相同调度和内存管理原语，但现在还包括：

  • x86 AVX-512
  • 手臂 AArch64
  • Apple Silicon（目前处于实验阶段）
  • IBM Z

OpenAI 兼容的 API 在后端之间是相同的，这意味着从 CPU 基础设施开始的部署可以迁移到 GPU，而无需更改应用程序层。

在 Arm 上，oneDNN 和 Arm 计算库构建路径与通过 llmcompressor 的 INT4 量化相结合，是在 AWS Graviton4 上测试的生产路径。

在 Intel 上，Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX) 在安装后会自动启用高级矩阵扩展 (AMX) 支持的 BF16 操作。 关键环境变量使操作员可以直接控制对 CPU 服务最重要的内存和线程权衡：

  • VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE（KV缓存分配，单位GB）
  • VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND（OpenMP 线程固定）
  • 实验性VLLM_CPU_SGL_KERNEL（AMX + BF16小批量内核）

结论

GPU 不会去任何地方。 对于大型模型的高并发生产服务，GPU 是正确的答案，并且将继续如此。

改变的是该语句的范围。 代理人工智能引入了一类工作负载——编排、工具执行、代码沙箱和多代理协调——其中 CPU 是完成这项工作的正确工具。 英特尔数据中心预测中的比率从 1:8 变为 1:1 并不是暂时的异常现象。 这一重大变化是推理变得迭代而不是单次的结果。

与此同时，边缘部署的经济性和限制（延迟、隐私、成本和离线可用性）推动了基于 CPU 的并行推理浪潮，适用于小型本地化模型，而 GPU 基础设施从来不适合这些模型。

NVIDIA 正在构建 Vera。 手臂跳回游戏。 英特尔至强的需求超过供应。 OpenAI 承包了数千万个 CPU。 CPU回来了。

接下来怎么办？

  • 在 OpenShift AI 上使用 vLLM 在 CPU 上部署模型：红帽是 vLLM 的主要贡献者，红帽 OpenShift AI 提供受支持的生产级平台，用于在 CPU 和 GPU 基础设施上提供模型服务，无论后端如何，都具有相同的 OpenAI 兼容 API。
  • 对您的 CPU 推理性能进行基准测试：使用开源 vllm-cpu-perf-eval 框架以及 GuideLLM 为您的硬件和工作负载建立可重复的基准。
